title: Property Superintendent
description:
Sutton Real Estate Company is seeking a Property Superintendent to be is responsible for the day-to-day maintenance, appearance, safety, and overall physical condition of properties managed by the real estate firm. This position serves as a hands-on representative of the company and works closely with property management, tenants, vendors, contractors, and service providers to ensure properties are well maintained, safe, clean, and operating efficiently.

The ideal candidate is dependable, mechanically inclined, organized, customer-service oriented, and comfortable working independently while managing multiple priorities.

Requirements

Property Maintenance & Operations:

  • Conduct routine inspections of assigned properties and identify maintenance, repair, safety, and cleanliness concerns.
  • Perform general building maintenance and minor repairs, including basic plumbing, electrical, carpentry, painting, drywall, doors, locks, fixtures, and other building components.
  • Maintain common areas, entrances, hallways, grounds, mechanical areas, and other property spaces in a clean, orderly, and presentable condition.
  • Monitor building systems and equipment and report issues requiring specialized service or major repair.
  • Respond promptly to maintenance requests, emergencies, and urgent property concerns.

  • Maintain appropriate inventory of maintenance supplies, tools, and equipment.
  • Assist with preparation of vacant units or spaces for new tenants, including cleaning, repairs, touch-ups, and general turnover work.

Vendor & Contractor Coordination

  • Coordinate with outside contractors, vendors, and service providers as directed by Property Management.
  • Provide access to properties for contractors and monitor work to ensure services are completed appropriately.
  • Report deficiencies, delays, or additional repair needs to Property Management.
  • Maintain professional relationships with vendors, tenants, and building occupants.

Tenant & Customer Service

  • Serve as a professional and responsive point of contact for routine property-related concerns.
  • Respond to tenant maintenance requests and communicate updates regarding the status of repairs.
  • Maintain a professional, courteous, and service-oriented approach when interacting with tenants and visitors.
  • Escalate tenant concerns, emergencies, or issues outside the scope of responsibility to Property Management.

Safety & Compliance

  • Conduct regular property walkthroughs to identify potential safety hazards, maintenance issues, or code-related concerns.
  • Immediately report significant safety concerns, property damage, water leaks, equipment failures, or other emergencies.
  • Follow all company policies and applicable safety requirements.
  • Assist with emergency response and property-related incidents when necessary.
  • Ensure maintenance activities are performed safely and appropriately.

Administrative Responsibilities

  • Maintain accurate records of completed maintenance, inspections, repairs, service calls, and property issues.
  • Communicate regularly with Property Management regarding property conditions, outstanding repairs, and anticipated maintenance needs.

  • Assist with property projects, inspections, move-ins, move-outs, and other operational activities as needed.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred.
  • Previous experience in property maintenance, building maintenance, facilities, construction, apartment maintenance, or a related field preferred.
  • General knowledge of plumbing, electrical, carpentry, HVAC, painting, drywall, and other basic building maintenance.
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and troubleshooting skills.
  • Ability to use common hand and power tools safely.
  • Ability to work independently and prioritize multiple maintenance requests.
  • Strong communication and customer-service skills.
  • Dependable, organized, and responsive.
  • Ability to interact professionally with tenants, vendors, contractors, and coworkers.
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation may be required.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, kneel, climb stairs, and work in various positions for extended periods.
  • Ability to lift and carry maintenance materials and equipment.
  • Ability to work indoors and outdoors in varying weather conditions.
  • Ability to safely use ladders and common maintenance tools and equipment.
  • Ability to respond to occasional after-hours emergencies, depending on property requirements.

Benefits

Schedule: Full-Time | Monday–Friday 7:00am – 3:30pm

This position will require on call rotation for on property needs and work order emergency situations.

Pay Rate: $25.00 - $28.00 per hour based on experience and qualifications.

title: Data Engineer - Spark
description:
Job Description

About the Role


The Data Platform team at Chargebee builds and maintains scalable data systems that power internal analytics, business intelligence, and customer-facing data features.

As a Data Engineer, you will work on building and maintaining reliable data pipelines across multiple layers of the data platform, including data ingestion, distributed processing, transformation, and data serving.


You will collaborate closely with product engineers, analysts, and platform teams to ensure that data is ingested, processed, and made available efficiently for analytics and product use cases. This role provides opportunities to work with modern data technologies and distributed systems, solving real-world data challenges at scale.


The team operates in a fast-paced and collaborative environment, building reliable and scalable infrastructure that supports Chargebee’s growing data needs.


What You Will Work On


As a Data Engineer, you will contribute to the development and evolution of Chargebee’s data platform. This includes working on systems responsible for ingesting large volumes of data, processing and transforming it using distributed systems like Apache Spark, and making it available for analytics and customer-facing products.


The role provides exposure to:


  • Large-scale data ingestion and processing pipelines
  • Streaming and event-driven architectures
  • Distributed data processing frameworks
  • Cloud-based data infrastructure
  • Building and maintaining data lake and data warehouses
  • Building data capabilities powering both internal analytics and customer-facing products


Key Responsibilities


  • Design, build, and maintain data ingestion and processing pipelines across multiple layers of the data platform.
  • Develop and optimize ETL/ELT workflows to support scalable and reliable data processing.
  • Build and maintain distributed data processing jobs using frameworks such as Apache Spark.
  • Work with streaming and queue-based systems such as Kafka to process event-driven data.
  • Design efficient data models and transformations to support analytics and product use cases.
  • Ensure high standards of data reliability, integrity, and performance across the data platform.
  • Troubleshoot and debug production data pipelines and distributed systems.
  • Collaborate with data analysts, product teams, and engineers to support evolving data requirements.
  • Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and agile development processes.
  • Document data pipelines, architecture decisions, and platform workflows.


Minimum Qualifications


  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 1–2 years of experience working with data processing workflows and pipelines.
  • Experience working on production systems, including troubleshooting and debugging technical issues.
  • Experience with distributed computing system such as Apace Spark.
  • Experience using Git workflows in collaborative development environments.
  • Strong knowledge of SQL.
  • Proficiency in at least one programming language such as Java, Python, or Scala.
  • Good understanding of data structures, data models, and relational database concepts.
  • Experience with relational databases such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, or similar.
  • Experience working in an Agile development environment.


Good-to-Have Qualifications


  • Experience working within the AWS ecosystem.
  • Experience building data pipelines using Apache Spark.
  • Familiarity with distributed data processing frameworks and large-scale data systems.
  • Understanding of data warehouse and data lake architectures.
  • Strong technical communication and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to investigate and debug issues across distributed systems.
  • Knowledge / prior experience on open table formats like - deltalake, iceberg or hudi

title: Applied History Research Coordinator
description:
The Belfer Center seeks a Research Coordinator to support the Belfer Center’s Applied History Project by conducting Applied History research and coordinating operations for the project. The Research Coordinator will report to the Associate Director of the Applied History Project.

The Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs is the hub of Harvard Kennedy School's research, teaching, and training in international security and diplomacy, environmental and resource issues, and science and technology policy. In 2021, the Belfer Center was named a “Center of Excellence” by the University of Pennsylvania’s Think Tanks and Civil Societies Program, in recognition of the Center’s six consecutive years as the world’s #1 university-affiliated think tank.

The Center has a dual mission: (1) to provide leadership in advancing policy-relevant knowledge about the most important challenges of international security and other critical issues where science, technology, environmental policy, and international affairs intersect; and (2) to prepare future generations of leaders for these arenas.

We believe that creating a diverse and inclusive organization is central to our ability to achieve our mission. It is our goal to promote historically underrepresented groups within our organization and within the fields of science and international affairs.


Job-Specific Responsibilities:

The Research Coordinator will play a key role in:

  • Tracking the activities of the worldwide Applied History network and writing the monthly Applied History Network Newsletter.

  • Conducting research on Applied History methods and supporting the production of instructional materials.

  • Conducting Applied History research on issues in U.S. foreign policy, international order, nuclear security, and the role of history in public life and higher education.

  • Coordinating logistics and supporting agenda development for private working group meetings and events for the Harvard community.

  • Assisting in the administration of the Ernest May Fellowship.

  • Managing the Applied History Project’s website and social media.

  • Other related job duties, as required.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree required.


Additional Qualifications and Skills:

  • Master’s degree in History is preferred, though we will consider candidates who have a bachelor’s degree with extraordinary academic or professional credentials.

  • 2+ years of related work experience preferred but not required.

  • Significant knowledge of, and interest in, international history, current international security issues, research methods, and higher education. Relevant coursework will count toward experience.

  • Exceptional writing skills, ability to remain organized, and competence coordinating logistics for events.

  • Demonstrated ability to work with minimal supervision under tight deadlines.

  • Appointment End Date: This is a fully benefits-eligible term appointment ending one year from date of hire with the possibility of renewal.
  • Standard Hours/Schedule: 35 hours per week
  • Visa Sponsorship Information: Harvard University is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position
  • Pre-Employment Screening: Identity, Education
  • Other Information: This is an in-person/on campus position based in Cambridge, MA, with possible flexible work options.

All applicants must submit the following as part of a complete application:

(1) Cover letter of 300 words or less

(2) Résumé or CV

(3) Official or unofficial transcript

(4) Analytic writing sample of 20 pages or less

(5) Names and contact information for three references

The first date of application review is October 10, 2026. After that, applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

Evaluation of qualified candidates may include a written assessment exercise which may be followed by competency-based interviews with Dr. Justin Winokur, the Associate Director of the Applied History Project, and Professor Graham Allison, the Director of the Applied History Project and the Douglas Dillon Professor of Government at the Harvard Kennedy School.

Work Format Details

This position has been determined by school or unit leaders that some of the duties and responsibilities can be effectively performed at a non-Harvard location. The work schedule and location will be set by the department at its discretion and based upon operational needs. When not working at a Harvard or Harvard-designated location, employees in hybrid positions must work in a Harvard registered state in compliance with the University’s Policy on Employment Outside of Massachusetts. Additional details will be discussed during the interview process. Certain visa types and funding sources may limit work location. Individuals must meet work location sponsorship requirements prior to employment.

Salary Grade and Ranges

This position is salary grade level 054. Please visit Harvard's Salary Ranges to view the corresponding salary range and related information.

Benefits

Harvard offers a comprehensive benefits package that is designed to support a healthy work-life balance and your physical, mental and financial wellbeing. Because here, you are what matters. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

  • Generous paid time off including parental leave
  • Medical, dental, and vision health insurance coverage starting on day one
  • Retirement plans with university contributions
  • Wellbeing and mental health resources
  • Support for families and caregivers
  • Professional development opportunities including tuition assistance and reimbursement
  • Commuter benefits, discounts and campus perks

title: Assistant Controller
description:
Start your career in Finance within an international software company where development, technology and AI are at the heart of how we work.

Have you recently graduated in Finance, Business Economics or Accountancy and are you ready to take your first professional step? Or have you already gained some initial work experience and are looking for an environment where you can continue to learn and grow?

For our Accounting & Control team, we are looking for an Assistant Controller who brings a solid foundation in Finance, is eager to learn and is curious about how technology and AI are changing the finance profession.

At Ultimo Group, you will work in an international software organisation with approximately 500 colleagues and operations in countries including the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, the United Kingdom and the United States. It is a great environment to start your career and gain experience in Finance within an international context from day one.

We do not expect you to know everything already. We are primarily looking for someone with a solid financial foundation, curiosity and the ambition to develop further. And we are happy to invest in that development.

We also believe that learning works both ways. Through your studies, internship, graduation project, previous job or personal interests, you may already have explored new technologies, AI tools or different ways of working that we have not yet considered. We value that fresh perspective. So bring your ideas: together, we will explore whether and how we can put them into practice.

Your role

As an Assistant Controller, you will have a broad role within our Accounting & Control team. You will contribute to financial administration, periodic closings, reporting, treasury and audits, giving you the opportunity to develop a strong understanding of different areas within Finance.

You will work alongside experienced colleagues who will support you and help you develop your professional skills. As your knowledge and experience grow, so will your independence and responsibilities.

At the same time, Ultimo is looking ahead. AI and automation create many opportunities to make processes more efficient, improve quality and reduce manual work. You will have the opportunity to actively contribute to this. You do not need to be an AI expert – curiosity and a willingness to experiment are much more important to us.

What will you do?

Within Accounting & Control, you will support activities including:

  • monthly, quarterly and year-end closings;
  • reviewing and processing financial data;
  • preparing balance sheet reconciliations and supporting schedules;
  • identifying and following up on discrepancies in the financial administration;
  • intercompany reconciliations between our international entities;
  • improving and further automating financial processes and internal controls.

Within Audit & Compliance, you will support external audits, prepare audit documentation and assist with CBS filings, statistical reporting and other finance and compliance-related activities.

Treasury will also be part of your role. You will support weekly payment runs, banking activities, cash flow reporting and liquidity management.

Finance, technology & AI

Finance is changing rapidly. We do not see AI and automation as something for the future, but as part of how we want to work today and tomorrow.

Together with the team, you will look at how processes can be improved. Which recurring activities can we automate? Where can AI support analysis or controls? And how can we make better use of our financial systems?

For us, innovation is not about using technology simply because it is new. It should help us work more efficiently, improve quality and make smarter decisions. If you have ideas, you will have the opportunity to explore and test them and, if they work, implement them together with the team.

Who are we looking for?

This role is a great fit if you have recently graduated and are looking for your first professional job. It is equally suitable if you have already gained some initial work experience and are ready for your next step.

We are looking for someone who:

  • has completed an MBO+/HBO-level degree in Finance, Business Economics, Accountancy or a comparable field;
  • has gained some practical experience in Finance or Accountancy through an internship, graduation project or first job;
  • works accurately and in a structured way and is interested in understanding what is behind the numbers;
  • has strong analytical skills and enjoys investigating and solving problems;
  • takes initiative and is comfortable asking questions;
  • is confident using Excel and comfortable learning new systems and technologies;
  • is interested in AI and automation;
  • communicates well in both Dutch and English, verbally and in writing.

Do you not yet have experience in every area listed above? Do not let that stop you from applying. We look at what you already bring, but just as importantly at your potential and where you want to grow.

Working and learning together

Our Finance team regularly works together from our office in Nunspeet. We offer flexibility and the opportunity to work partly hybrid, but we also believe there is real value in spending time together as a team.

Especially at the beginning of your career, you can learn a great deal simply by working alongside experienced colleagues: asking a quick question, looking at something together, solving a problem as a team or seeing how a colleague approaches a challenge.

And, to be fair, it is also simply more enjoyable!

You will not be placed behind a laptop and expected to figure everything out by yourself. You will become part of a team where people help each other, share knowledge and take responsibility for results together.

What do we offer?

We believe a strong start to your career should combine interesting work, opportunities to develop and competitive employment conditions.

You can expect:

  • a gross annual salary between €50,000 and €60,000, depending on your knowledge and experience;
  • an attractive annual bonus scheme;
  • a strong pension plan;
  • a €60 net monthly internet allowance;
  • modern equipment and high-quality tools to do your job;
  • flexibility and the opportunity to work partly hybrid;
  • plenty of opportunities to continue developing professionally.

You may start as an Assistant Controller, but we like to look beyond your first role. As your knowledge and experience grow, we will explore together what your next step could be within Accounting & Control, Finance or another financial specialisation that fits your strengths and ambitions.

Interested?

We are not looking for an experienced Controller with a ten-page CV. We are looking for someone with a solid foundation, curiosity, ambition and the motivation to build a professional career within an international software organisation.

Someone who wants to learn from us, but who will also occasionally surprise us with an idea that makes us think: why weren’t we already doing it this way?

Recognise yourself in this? We would love to meet you.

title: Salesforce Education Cloud Consultant
description:
We believe in the power of ingenuity to build a positive human future. We challenge where it matters and own the outcome. We combine strategic thinking, customer-centric service design, and agile engineering practices to accelerate innovation in a tech-driven world.

Why consider joining our Digital & Data community? 🤔

  • Join our Digital & Data team working alongside product, design and a wide range of other experts and cross-disciplinary teams to bring ideas to life through innovative software solutions.
  • Grow a flexible and unique career within a trust-based, inclusive environment that values excellence, innovation, and curiosity. You have the option to progress with us on a technical career track. No need to go onto the Partner career track if this doesn’t align with what you want to do.
  • Hybrid working - our approach is to be in the office or on client site a minimum of 2 days per week.
  • Work on a broad variety of projects and tech stacks for clients across seven sectors - no project is ever the same
  • Join other experts within our supportive and collaborative tech community through knowledge-sharing and peer-level support, coaching and mentoring

The Role

We are investing in a strategic Salesforce Higher Education practice and are looking for an experienced Salesforce Education Cloud Consultant to help shape its growth and success.

Working with leading universities and higher education providers, you will deliver impactful Salesforce solutions that improve student experiences, strengthen institutional engagement and support long-term digital transformation. You will combine strong Salesforce expertise with consulting skills and sector knowledge to become a trusted advisor to our clients and a key contributor to our growing Salesforce capability.

You will:

  • Lead requirements gathering, discovery workshops and stakeholder engagement activities across Higher Education transformation programmes.
  • Design and deliver Salesforce Education Cloud solutions that support recruitment, admissions, enrolment, student success, wellbeing and alumni engagement.
  • Work with clients to challenge existing processes, identify opportunities for improvement and define future-state operating models.
  • Configure and implement Salesforce solutions, working closely with architects, developers and delivery teams.
  • Support programmes that utilise the wider Salesforce ecosystem, including Experience Cloud, Service Cloud and other Salesforce platform capabilities.
  • Help clients establish connected digital ecosystems through integration with Student Record Systems, Learning Management Systems, identity management platforms and enterprise applications.
  • Support data migration, data quality and governance activities to ensure successful platform adoption and long-term business value.
  • Build trusted relationships with client stakeholders by providing expert advice on Salesforce capabilities, industry best practice and platform strategy.
  • Contribute to bids, proposals, demonstrations and client presentations, helping grow our Salesforce Higher Education practice.
  • Contribute to the development of reusable assets and delivery accelerators that improve delivery quality and strengthen our reputation within the Higher Education sector.
  • Share knowledge and support the development of junior team members where appropriate.

Essential requirements ✅

  • Salesforce Certified Education Cloud Consultant.
  • Salesforce Administrator certification.
  • Experience delivering Salesforce implementation programmes in a consultant, business analyst or functional consultant capacity.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Salesforce Education Cloud.
  • Experience working with Higher Education institutions or education-focused transformation programmes.
  • Strong understanding of the student lifecycle, including recruitment, admissions, enrolment, retention, student support and alumni engagement.
  • Proven ability to facilitate workshops, gather requirements and translate business needs into effective Salesforce solutions.
  • Experience working with business and technical stakeholders at multiple levels of an organisation.
  • Experience supporting data migration, integration and change adoption activities.
  • Understanding of Salesforce DevOps and CI/CD practices, including source control, release management and deployment tools such as Git, Azure DevOps, Copado or Gearset.
  • Strong communication, stakeholder management and consulting skills.
  • A pragmatic, outcome-focused approach to solving complex business challenges.

Desirable

  • Certifications in Business Analyst, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, Marketing Cloud, AI Associate, Agentforce Specialist or Platform Developer I.
  • Experience delivering solutions across the Salesforce platform, including Experience Cloud and Service Cloud. Exposure to Data Cloud, Agentforce and Marketing Cloud would be advantageous.
  • Experience integrating Salesforce with enterprise platforms using MuleSoft, Azure Integration Services, Boomi or similar middleware technologies.
  • Exposure to AI-enabled customer, student or employee engagement solutions.
  • Experience working with Higher Education platforms including Tribal SITS, Ellucian Banner, Moodle, Canvas, Blackboard or similar solutions.
  • Experience with reporting and analytics technologies such as Power BI, Tableau.
  • Experience working within a consulting, systems integration or professional services environment.

Personal Attributes

  • Passionate about helping universities transform the student experience.
  • Naturally curious, commercially aware and motivated by solving meaningful client challenges.
  • Able to build credibility quickly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Collaborative, adaptable and comfortable working in fast-paced delivery environments.
  • Committed to delivery excellence and creating lasting value for clients.
  • Excited by the opportunity to help build and grow a market-leading Salesforce Higher Education practice.

Assessment process ⚖️

title: Associate Director of Research Core Finance and Compliance
description:
Job Summary: Lead financial operations and planning for the department/unit that may include payroll, accounting, accounts payable/receivable, procurement, capital projects, endowment funding, research administration, or other function.

Job-Specific Responsibilities:

The Associate Director of Research Core Finance and Compliance partners with the Director Research Core Finance and Compliance to provide strategic financial leadership, oversight, and compliance support for FAS Science service centers and recharge facilities. The Associate Director serves as a key financial resource to core facility directors, divisional leadership, and other stakeholders, ensuring sound financial management, transparent reporting, and compliance with University and federal requirements.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Partners with the Director to lead financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and analysis for FAS Science service centers and recharge facilities.
  • Provides strategic financial guidance to core facility directors, divisional leadership, and senior management to support operational and long-range decision-making.
  • Leads the annual budget and forecasting processes in accordance with FAS Finance policies, procedures, and timelines.
  • Serves as a subject matter expert on core facility financial management, including operating and capital budgets, rate development, cost recovery, and short- and long-range financial projections.
  • Develops financial analyses, dashboards, and management reports to identify trends, assess financial performance, and inform strategic and operational decisions.
  • Prepares annual and ad hoc financial reports, business plans, and scenario analyses related to cost recovery, equipment replacement, service expansion, and other strategic initiatives.
  • Partners with core facility directors and divisional leadership to establish appropriate service center and recharge rates.
  • Develops, maintains, and continuously improves rate-setting methodologies, financial models, and standardized templates.
  • Conducts annual reviews of rates and financial performance to ensure compliance with federal requirements and Harvard service center policies.
  • Develops, implements, and continuously improves policies, procedures, workflows, and internal controls related to the financial operations and accounting of Science Division core facilities.
  • Establishes and monitors accounting practices and control mechanisms to ensure compliance with University financial policies and applicable federal service center regulations.
  • Reviews financial activity and transactions to identify compliance risks, financial issues, and opportunities for process improvement.
  • Oversees and enhances service center billing, accounts receivable, and related financial operations to improve accuracy, efficiency, and timely revenue collection.
  • Develops and maintains core facility charts of accounts and financial structures that promote transparency, consistency, accurate reporting, and increased reporting automation.
  • Identifies opportunities to standardize and streamline financial processes across core facilities and implements tools and practices that improve efficiency, financial visibility, and internal controls.
  • May supervise and develop staff responsible for financial operations, analysis, billing, or related functions and provide guidance to staff and stakeholders across the Science Division.

Working Conditions:

  • This position will be based on our campus in Cambridge, MA, with the possibility of having a hybrid in-person/remote schedule. The selected candidate will need to be on campus as business needs require. Specific days and hours will be determined between you and your manager.

  • Minimum of seven years of relevant experience in finance, accounting, research administration, financial operations, or a related field.
  • MBA, master’s degree, or other advanced degree in finance, accounting, business administration, or a related field preferred.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, accounting, and financial operations.
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel and experience developing complex financial models and analyses.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate complex financial information into clear recommendations for varied audiences.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and improve financial processes, policies, internal controls, and reporting tools.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively with senior leaders, faculty, administrators, and operational teams.
  • Experience managing multiple priorities and projects in a complex, decentralized organization preferred.
  • Knowledge of service center, recharge center, sponsored research, or higher education financial practices preferred.
  • Familiarity with federal cost principles and compliance requirements applicable to research service centers is strongly preferred.
  • The successful candidate will be a collaborative and strategic financial professional who combines strong technical expertise with sound judgment, attention to detail, and a commitment to continuous improvement.
  • The role requires the ability to balance financial stewardship and regulatory compliance with the operational and strategic needs of research core facilities.

description:

Help Us Build Relationships That Help Families

HomeWell Care Services is seeking a confident, relationship-focused professional with at least one year of relevant experience to expand our presence throughout North Jacksonville and Nassau County, including Callahan, Yulee, and Fernandina Beach.

This is not a position for someone who drops off brochures.

We are looking for someone who can confidently walk into hospitals, rehabilitation facilities, senior living communities, physician offices, and professional organizations, identify the right decision-makers, and begin developing genuine referral relationships.

You will represent a locally owned home care agency helping older adults and individuals maintain their independence, safety, and quality of life at home.

  • Follow targeted weekly outreach routes developed with agency leadership
  • Identify discharge planners, social workers, case managers, administrators, and referral decision makers

Successful performance includes consistent completion of outreach routes, meaningful conversations with referral decision makers, new qualified contacts, follow-up meetings with high-potential partners, accurate same-day documentation, and demonstrated movement of relationships from introductions to active opportunities.

We value the quality and progression of relationships—not simply the number of brochures distributed.

You are confident, warm, professional, personable, and persistent. You are comfortable speaking with healthcare and business professionals and can independently manage routes, contacts, and follow-up commitments.

You should be motivated by measurable goals and personal accountability, communicate clearly in person, by phone, and in writing, and be comfortable using mobile applications and basic CRM/tracking systems.

  • Healthcare marketing or business development

  • Community outreach
  • Medical or pharmaceutical sales
  • Relationship management or outside sales
  • Veterans' services or senior service organizations

  • Ability to travel throughout the assigned territory

  • Flexible weekday scheduling
  • Performance-based bonus opportunities after the introductory period

  • Opportunity to grow into a larger business development or leadership role as the agency expands
Why HomeWell?

HomeWell Care Services is locally operated and committed to providing dependable, compassionate care to families throughout our community.

We believe relationships are built through consistency, responsiveness, and trust. We are looking for someone who takes ownership, follows through on commitments, and understands that every professional relationship could eventually help a family find the support they need.

If you are energized by meeting people, opening doors, and building something meaningful in your community, we would like to meet you.

Job Type: Part-Time, W-2

Schedule: Weekday day shift with occasional community events
Work Location: On the road throughout North Jacksonville and Nassau County

title: People Lead
description:
People Lead

About the role

We are hiring River AI’s first People Lead to own the human resources function and the related systems that keep the company running: HR, payroll, benefits, insurance, and operations. You'll set them up, run them day to day, and keep improving them as we grow.

The role has unusual reach. You will shape nearly everyone's experience here, from a new hire's first day to the environment every employee works in, and you will be trusted with the judgment calls that come with that.

We are a team that is genuinely interested in working smarter. You will have real room to deploy AI to take the repetitive or tedious parts of operations off your plate, so your time goes to meaningful work.

Who we are

title: LifeSet Case Worker
description:
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

The YVLifeSet Case Worker provides individual services to 6-8 young adults, ages Eighteen (18) to twenty-one (21) in the home and community setting to assist the young adult with transition to adulthood, meeting a minimum of one time per week face to face with the young person and providing additional support via phone, text, or in person as needed.


When indicated, a YVLifeSet Case Worker may see a young person daily to ensure safety and stability. Additionally, the YVLifeSet Case Worker is directly responsible for all interventions associated with a specific young adult and their family. This includes case management and collaboration with external key stakeholders and referral sources, such as probation, child welfare workers, therapists, etc. The specialist conducts ongoing assessment of the young person’s needs from a strength focused, solution-based perspective and develops service plans on a monthly basis. The specialist also documents all service contacts with the young adult within the timelines required by the organization.


The Case Worker is expected to attend all meetings related to the young adult and/or family with the purpose of gathering information specific to intervention development and advocating in the best interest of the young adult’s long-term stability.

The Case Specialist is on call 24/7 (rotating on-call at night and on weekends) and expected to respond in person at any time when it is determined to be necessary by the Team supervisor, clinical consultant and program director.


In addition, the Case Worker is expected to attend and actively participate in individual and team supervision sessions and trainings and to follow up and/or implement feedback and recommendations received from the team supervisor, program director, and clinical consultant. The specialist is expected to adhere to all ethical and legal guidelines, including confidentiality and mandated reporting.


RESPONSIBILITIES:

· Document all case management activity and use information in up-to-date case entry notes

· Promotes a youth guided, family centered, and strengths-based environment at all times

· Assists youth in developing family resources or adult’s connections.

· Write and submit timely reports for juvenile court and administrative case reviews, etc.

· Takes leadership in the planning and evaluation of staffing’s/conferences

· Takes responsibility for presenting intake material to employees and presenting to Intake Committee for final decision as applicable

· Provides data, information, and goals to team. Works with treatment, collateral staff, and families in coordinating efforts to reach goals

· Requires knowledge of typical child and adolescent development and an understanding of trauma exposure and traumatic stress signs and symptoms.

· Practice will include using strategies that support healing, recovery, and that resist re-traumatization

· Engage caregivers, parents, family members and others by sharing strengths and challenges experienced by program participants

· Attends agency and other professional seminars and conferences to increase professional knowledge and skills

· Liaison to DCFS or other agencies (courts, school districts, etc.), communicating goals and progress toward their accomplishment

· May provide counseling (if appropriate)

· Locates and evaluates resources, facilitates referrals and supportive services

· May cover ACR/court and other duties during employee vacancies/absences

· Documents contact with young people, family, court sessions, etc. for statistical purposes

· Uses active and reflective listening skills and affirmations to demonstrate respect and empathy, avoiding negative and derogatory labels that foster disrespect

· Understand that behaviors, responses, attitudes, and emotions are a collection of survival skills often developed in response to traumatic experiences

· Maintain confidentiality of employees, volunteers, and program participants to provide a safe environment

· Attend at least two trainings related to being trauma informed in a twelve-month period

· Ability to work effectively with program participants and family members, employees and vendors in a culturally diverse environment to support healing and recovery

· Participates in the development and implementation of continuous quality improvement activities as assigned

· Other duties as assigned.

title: Director of Institutional Research
description: The Director of Institutional Research serves as a visionary, service-minded intelligence leader and trusted advisor to campus executives. The Director leads the transformation of institutional data into actionable, forward-looking insights that drive strategic growth, institutional effectiveness, as program, faculty, and student success. Grounded in a culture of collaborative service and relationship-building, this role bridges business intelligence with institutional strategy, fostering strong cross-functional partnerships, championing proactive decision-making, and navigating the evolving higher education landscape. DUTIES RESPONSIBILITIES Visionary Leadership Relationship Building Strategic Partnership: Build trust-based, collaborative relationships across academic and administrative units, deans, and campus leaders to proactively identify data needs and deliver consultative insights. Cross-Institutional Alignment: Partner actively with IR offices across the UL System and external networks to benchmark innovative practices, harmonize data definitions, and champion collaborative higher education research. Strategic Data Translation Storytelling: Guide the synthesis, analysis, and compelling presentation of complex data into clear, actionable resources, reports, and high-impact special projects for executive leadership and campus stakeholders—translating raw metrics into meaningful strategic narratives. Service-Minded Culture: Cultivate a customer-centric, accessible, and supportive environment within the Office of IR, positioning the team as a go-to partner for strategic problem-solving. Coalition Governance Leadership: Chair and guide key governance groups, including the Data Governance Committee, Data Standards Committee, and work with data visualization experts to inspire shared data stewardship and collaborative decision-making. Serve as a member of the Data Governance Committee, as well as represent the Office of IR in meetings or committees for institutional reporting and data needs. Strategic Intelligence Forward-Thinking Analytics Predictive Proactive Insights: Shift institutional research from historical reporting to forward-thinking predictive modeling, trend forecasting, and scenario planning to anticipate institutional opportunities and risks. Modern Business Intelligence: Drive the expansion of modern data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau) and interactive dashboards to empower campus stakeholders with self-service analytics and KPI tracking. Digital Presence Data Transparency: Oversee the IR website to ensure it serves as a dynamic, user-friendly hub for institutional intelligence; curate public-facing dashboards, fact books, accountability metrics, and strategic plan tracking; and maintain accessible resources that promote campus-wide data literacy. Environmental Scanning: Synthesize higher education trends, demographic shifts, and regional benchmarks to inform long-range strategic planning and enrollment strategies. Data Enablement Campus Literacy: Design and lead campus-wide training programs, workshops, and user-friendly resources that empower faculty, staff, and leadership to effectively navigate analytics platforms (e.g., Tableau, Qualtrics, Ellucian Insight), interpret data accurately, and build confidence in data-informed decision-making. Data Strategy, Governance Ecosystem Modernization Ethical Data Stewardship Integrity: Collaborate with the Enterprise Data Governance Planning Committee to establish modern data standards, ethical AI/data usage policies, and robust security controls. Ensure appropriate, ethical, and compliant use of data on behalf of the university. Embed the standard of ethical practice as defined by AIR. ( https://www.airweb.org/resources/publications/statement-of-ethical-principles/principles ) Data Infrastructure Elevation: Guide the continuous optimization of data pipelines, operational data storage systems, and analytics platforms to ensure seamless data delivery, both internally and with system partners. Strategic Survey Administration Governance: Oversee the campus-wide scheduling, design, and administration of institutional surveys using enterprise tools (Qualtrics); enforce policy compliance, survey fatigue mitigation, and best practices; and govern the appropriate use of institutional distribution lists to safeguard data integrity and student/employee privacy. Mandatory Regulatory Excellence: Direct accurate and timely compliance reporting (Board of Regents, NCES/IPEDS, U.S. News, external rankings) and serve as the primary liaison for System-level shared resources. Coordinate campus data validation, subject-matter expertise, approvals and institutional context to ensure accurate and timely submissions. Team Development Operational Stewardship Professional Thought Leadership Horizon Scanning: Actively engage with regional and national professional associations (e.g., AIR, SAIR, LAIR) through conference attendance, network participation, and scholarly research to track emerging higher education trends, modern analytics methodologies, and advanced IR technologies—ensuring the university remains at the forefront of data-informed leadership. Project Management Tracking: Prioritize and manage data requests through clear intake criteria; track and communicate project milestones transparently to stakeholders; and foster a culture of continuous operational improvement. Talent Empowerment: Mentor and develop a modern, growth-oriented IR team, fostering a supportive, innovative, and continuous-learning workplace culture. Resource Management: Strategically deploy financial and technological resources to maximize the impact of the IR office on campus priorities.

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
Job Description

Introduction: We at Entiovi Technologies provide digital transformation using new-age intelligent technologies for more than 9 years. We have clients located primarily in the US and Europe that are served by our Dedicated teams. This job is part of our expansion in India. Location: Remote About the role: The Senior Data Engineer in our AI & Data team will be responsible for designing and building the data structures and pipelines our AI Engineers rely on across Azure , Snowflake , Databricks , and Lakebase (our managed Postgres / OLTP layer). The primary mission of this role is to enable the AI Engineering team by translating the needs of machine-learning and computer-vision workflows into reliable, well-modelled, and cost-effective data foundations. Tasks include setting up new data pipelines and transformations, ingesting structured and unstructured data into the data lake and warehouse, monitoring the performance and cost-effectiveness of existing data jobs, and docking machine-learning processes into the existing data landscape. The Data Engineer works hand in hand with AI Engineers and is the go-to person for making trusted data available for models, products, and analytics. Main Responsibilities As part of the AI & Data team, design and build the data structures, schemas, and models that AI Engineers depend on for training, feature engineering, and inference. Strong experience in Data Architecture. Strong knowledge of Git repositories. Develop and orchestrate scalable data pipelines on Databricks (Spark, Delta Lake) and load curated, analytics-ready data into Snowflake . Own data ingestion, transformation (ELT/ETL), and storage across the Azure cloud (e.g. ADLS, Data Factory, Event Hubs / Synapse), including structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data such as text, images, and video. Dock machine-learning and computer-vision models into the data pipelines and design the data flow that feeds and consumes those AI services. Sync curated lakehouse data into Lakebase (managed Postgres) for low-latency serving, manage change-data-capture back into Delta tables, and support online feature stores and agent state for AI Engineers. Strong API knowledge and experience. Build and maintain API integrations and automated data ingestion from internal systems and external third-party sources. Monitor pipeline performance, reliability, and cost; troubleshoot failed jobs and optimize Snowflake and Databricks workloads. Implement data quality, validation, and lineage, and document the data dictionary and ETL processes. Partner with AI Engineers and stakeholders to translate model and business requirements into extensions of the data platform. Skills, Qualifications & Education Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, or a related field. At least 4 years of work experience in data engineering or a similar data-focused role. Hands-on production experience with Databricks (Apache Spark, Delta Lake, notebooks, workflows). Hands-on production experience with Snowflake (data modelling, performance tuning, access control, cost management). Solid experience with Microsoft Azure data services (e.g. ADLS, Data Factory, Event Hubs / Synapse). Experience with PostgreSQL and OLTP databases; familiarity with Lakebase (Databricks-managed Postgres) is a strong plus. Working knowledge of JavaScript / TypeScript , used for data APIs, microservices, or app-facing integrations. Strong expertise in SQL (will be tested during the recruitment process). Robust Python literacy, especially for data handling and pipeline development. Comfortable working with both structured and unstructured data; does not shy away from troubleshooting failed ETL processes or API integrations. Outstanding data-structure and data-modelling design skills. Working knowledge of machine-learning, NLP, or computer-vision workflows is a plus. Experience with dbt, Airflow, or Databricks Workflows, and with CI/CD and infrastructure-as-code, is a plus. Strong ability to translate ideas between technical and non-technical audiences. Curious, collaborative, self-motivated, and organized; able to run multiple projects against tight deadlines. Location: Remote

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
Job Description

Who We Are: AssetMark is a leading wealth management platform dedicated to empowering financial advisors and the investors they serve. As we continue to expand our global capabilities, we are establishing a Global Capability Center (GCC) in Hyderabad to enhance our operational excellence, strengthen strategic capabilities, and support our long-term growth. We are seeking an experienced Data Engineer to join the Billing team in Hyderabad. Billing is a business-critical and highly sensitive area where data accuracy, reliability, traceability, and on-time delivery are essential. You will build and operate data pipelines, curated data assets, and integrations that support time-sensitive billing processes and downstream consumers. The Opportunity We are seeking an experienced Data Engineer to join the Billing team in Hyderabad. Billing is a business-critical and highly sensitive area where data accuracy, reliability, traceability, and on-time delivery are essential. You will build and operate data pipelines, curated data assets, and integrations that support time-sensitive billing processes and downstream consumers. You will work primarily in Microsoft Azure with Databricks, Python, PySpark, SQL, and ETL/ELT patterns, using ActiveBatch for orchestration and scheduling. The role includes integrations with internal systems and third-party providers through APIs, databases, and file-based interfaces, as well as ownership of data hub and curation processes that must be complete, accurate, and delivered within narrow processing windows. The Billing team operates with a high quality bar and limited tolerance for delay. When production issues occur, the engineer is expected to investigate quickly, communicate clearly, implement safe corrective actions within the active processing window, and propose practical alternatives when the original approach is blocked. Strong judgment, prioritization, and time management are critical to success in this role. Snowflake is expected to become part of the future-state ecosystem, so prior Snowflake exposure is useful but is not a requirement for the current role. This role is based in Hyderabad and follows a hybrid work model. You will collaborate with colleagues across India and the United States, with reasonable working-hour overlap when needed for team ceremonies, planning, production support, and delivery. Key Responsibilities Billing Data Engineering: Design, build, test, deploy, and maintain reliable ETL/ELT pipelines and reusable data components in Azure and Databricks using Python, PySpark, and SQL. Data Hub & Curation: Transform source data into trusted, billing-ready curated datasets. Maintain consistent business rules, source-to-target traceability, and accurate delivery across data hub and curation layers. Data Quality & Reconciliation: Implement rigorous automated validations and reconciliations for completeness, accuracy, consistency, duplicates, referential integrity, and expected volumes. Treat data quality defects as production-impacting issues and resolve them with urgency. Orchestration & Scheduling: Develop and support ActiveBatch schedules, dependencies, execution chains, reruns, and recovery procedures. Ensure pipelines complete within narrow billing windows and downstream delivery commitments. Third-Party & Internal Integrations: Build and operate integrations with third-party providers and internal systems using APIs, databases, secure file transfers, and other appropriate interfaces. Design for retries, recoverability, idempotency, and clear failure handling. Production Reliability & Incident Response: Monitor pipeline execution and data delivery; investigate failures, data anomalies, and missed dependencies immediately. Apply safe in-window fixes or workarounds when necessary, communicate impact and status, and follow through with root-cause and permanent corrective actions. Performance & Timeliness: Optimize jobs and workflows to meet strict processing deadlines. Identify bottlenecks early, manage competing priorities, and escalate risks before they threaten billing timelines. Problem Solving & Alternatives: Break down ambiguous technical and data issues methodically, validate assumptions, and propose alternative implementation paths when constraints or dependencies prevent the preferred solution. Business & Technical Collaboration: Partner with Billing, Operations, Product, engineering, data, and other stakeholders to clarify requirements, understand business rules, communicate tradeoffs, and translate needs into dependable technical solutions. Security & Sensitive Data Handling: Follow secure engineering and data-handling practices for sensitive financial and billing data, including least-privilege access, appropriate controls, auditability, and protection of confidential information. Engineering Practices: Use Git-based workflows, code reviews, automated testing, deployment standards, documentation, and maintainable design patterns. Build solutions that can be supported under production time pressure without sacrificing quality. Continuous Improvement: Improve pipeline reliability, operational runbooks, test coverage, observability, recovery procedures, and team knowledge sharing based on production learnings and recurring failure patterns. Knowledge, Skills, Abilities Strong hands-on experience with Databricks for production data engineering workloads. Strong Python and PySpark skills for data transformation, automation, validation, troubleshooting, and operational support. title: Peer Advocate - SJO
description:

Position Purpose:

The Peer Advocate will participate as a valued member within the interdisciplinary team responsible for providing comprehensive health and social services to clients at Wesley Health Centers-San Julian Oasis (SJO) Program. Additionally, this position involves collaboration with the health education and prevention team. Through this collaboration, the Peer advocate will deliver practical information and personal insights from life experiences, aimed at assisting clients facing similar life challenges at Wesley Health Centers.

Program Population:

The SJO Recuperative Care Program consists of a cohesive team of clinicians, community health workers, and other professionals who collaborate to provide housing and critical services to People Experiencing Homelessness (PEH) and those who have previously experienced homelessness. The clients/patients may come with behavioral and/or substance abuse issues. The program utilizes the Harm Reduction Model and we “do whatever it takes” to encourage success of the client.

Principal Responsibilities:

  1. Foster a strong rapport with clients, demonstrating genuine care for their well-being.
  2. Provide unwavering support to clients, effectively motivating them to embrace behavior modification programs.
  3. Maintain strict, up-to-date, and confidential records detailing client progress in evolving personal behaviors.
  4. Initiate contact with clients once or twice monthly during scheduled hours.
  5. Accompany clients to referrals for health and social services, diligently encouraging adherence and strict recording advancements using appropriate documentation.
  6. Facilitate referrals to substance abuse recovery services, healthcare facilities, family planning services, and relevant social service organizations.
  7. Deliver approved curriculum-based educational content and skill-building information.
  8. Share personal experiences related to incarceration, substance abuse, mental health, and other associated risk behaviors.
  9. Assist in the continuous collection of program data and the processing of program-related forms.
  10. Contribute to the preparation of monthly reports for funding agencies.
  11. Fulfill any additional assigned duties.

Requirements:

  1. Proven experience in working with homeless individuals.
  2. Possession of a High School diploma or GED.
  3. Exceptional communication skills tailored to effectively engage homeless individuals grappling with substance abuse and other homelessness-associated factors.
  4. Personal triumph over challenges similar to those faced by clients.
  5. Ability to reliably travel to various community sites and punctually attend appointments.
  6. Strong desire to make a difference in the lives of homeless individuals.

*All JWCH, Wesley Health Centers workforce members are recommended to be fully vaccinated against COVID-19.

The Electrical Engineer is responsible for the design, development, testing, and support of electrical systems and subsystems used in medical devices. Working as part of a multidisciplinary product development team, this role contributes to the design of analog, digital, and power electronics, printed circuit boards (PCBs), cable assemblies, and related electrical components from concept through commercialization.

The incumbent develops and maintains electrical design documentation, supports prototype and production builds, collaborates with suppliers and manufacturing partners, and participates in verification, validation, and troubleshooting activities. The Electrical Engineer also contributes to product risk management, electrical safety and EMC compliance testing, and the investigation and resolution of product issues identified during internal testing or in the field.

This role plays a key part in ensuring product quality, reliability, and regulatory compliance by maintaining design documentation, supporting quality system requirements, and contributing to the development of safe and effective medical technologies that improve patient outcomes.

Duties:

  • Using the product requirement as inputs, support design for electrical circuits and subsystems of the company’s medical products, including power circuits, analog circuits and digital circuits

  • Participate in the creation and execution of test protocols
  • Create manufacturing test instructions as well as test jigs
  • Investigate issues identified in internal testing and at customer sites; participate in the resolution of the issues and deployment of the solutions
  • Participate in the certification of the company’s product to electrical safety standards (e.g. IEC 60601-1) and electromagnetic compatibility standards (IEC 60601-1-2)
  • Participate in risk management activities
  • Create and maintain documentation required to demonstrate compliance with the company’s QMS and all applicable medical device regulations
  • Adhere to and enhance the Quality Management System (QMS), including developing and maintaining documentation and training other staff as appropriate

Education:

  • B.ASc, B.Sc, or B.Eng in electrical or electronics engineering, or similar degree
  • Master’s degree in electrical or electronics engineering considered an asset

Experience:

  • 4+ years experience in electrical system design, including PCB schematic and layout
  • Experience in circuit testing and diagnostic methods, managing designs for production (DFM, obsolescence review)
  • Experience working within a Quality Management System is an asset
  • Exposure to mechanical engineering and integrating fixtures and components is an asset
  • Experience with embedded firmware, ideally C/C++, is an asset

Skills:

  • Knowledge of digital and analog circuit design
  • Knowledge of power distribution circuits (power supplies, isolation transformers, etc.)
  • Knowledge of electrical design and board layout software (OrCAD, Altium or other)
  • General knowledge of electrical safety standards (IEC 60601-1), electromagnetic compatibility concepts and standards
  • Excellent troubleshooting skills
  • Good verbal and written communication skills
  • Independent motivation and drive to achieve results, ability to work with minimal supervision
  • Knowledge of embedded software development (in C or other low-level language) an asset
  • Experience with STM32 platform an asset
  • Knowledge of IEC 62304 software standard and regulations governing medical device software an asset
  • Experience with 3D CAD software, cable management is an asset

What We Offer

  • Opportunity to work at the forefront of organ transplantation innovation.
  • Direct interaction with leading transplant programs across North America.
  • Exposure to clinical development, product commercialization, and medical education.
  • Collaborative, mission-driven environment focused on improving patient outcomes.
  • Competitive salary, benefits, and opportunities for professional growth.

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
At Zimmer Biomet, we believe in pushing the boundaries of innovation and driving our mission forward. As a global medical technology leader for nearly 100 years, a patient’s mobility is enhanced by a Zimmer Biomet product or technology every 8 seconds.

As a Zimmer Biomet team member, you will share in our commitment to providing mobility and renewed life to people around the world. To support our talent team, we focus on development opportunities, robust employee resource groups (ERGs), a flexible working environment, location specific competitive total rewards, wellness incentives and a culture of recognition and performance awards. We are committed to creating an environment where every team member feels included, respected, empowered and recognised.


What You Can Expect

The Senior Data Engineer is responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining scalable data pipelines and models within Snowflake and cloud environments. This role combines strong SQL and Python development with hands-on data engineering in Agile teams. The engineer will partner with architects, analysts, and business teams to deliver secure, reliable, high-quality data solutions that power analytics, reporting, and operational workflows.


Work Location: Bangalore
Work Mode: Hybrid (3 Days in office)
Shift Timing - 3:00 PM - 12:00 AM

How You'll Create Impact

- Design, build, and optimize SQL pipelines, transformations, and data models within Snowflake.
- Develop Python-based data processing, automation, and integration workflows.
- Ingest and process structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data from databases, APIs, files, SaaS applications, and cloud storage.
- Implement ETL/ELT processes using SQL, Python, dbt, Snowflake features, or orchestration tools such as Airflow/Dagster.
- Contribute to Agile ceremonies and deliverables, ensuring timely and high-quality sprint outcomes.
- Implement CI/CD workflows and maintain version-controlled repositories (GitHub or equivalent).
- Support data governance, data quality, and secure data handling practices.
- Troubleshoot pipeline issues and proactively drive performance improvements.
- Maintain documentation, monitoring, alerting, and operational playbooks for pipelines.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Data Engineering, Architecture, Data Science, Business) to translate requirements into technical solutions.


Technologies Required for Role (REQUIRED FIELD)

• SQL (strong expertise), Snowflake is a plus, and data modeling
• Python for data pipelines and automation
• dbt / SQL-based transformation frameworks (preferred)
• Airflow, Dagster, or similar orchestration tools
• CI/CD tools (GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps)
• ETL/ELT tools such as Fivetran, Airbyte, Apache Nifi
• Cloud services (AWS, Azure, GCP) and cloud storage
• Git-based version control.

What Makes You Stand Out

• Ability to work effectively within cross-functional and Agile teams.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills.
• Experience working with US- and Europe-based clients, stakeholders, or team members is desired.
• Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate technical information for non-technical partners.
• Strong organizational skills with attention to detail and documentation.
• Ability to influence and collaborate across teams and geographies.
• Demonstrated ownership, adaptability, and willingness to embrace new technologies.
• Ability to understand and work across multiple technology stacks.

Your Background

- 7 + years of experience designing and developing SQL-based pipelines and data models.
- Hands-on experience with Python for ETL/ELT development and automation.
- Experience with Snowflake or other cloud data warehouses.
- Experience with orchestration platforms such as Airflow, Dagster, or Prefect.
- Experience with ingestion tools (Fivetran, Airbyte) is a plus.
- Familiarity with APIs, JSON/CSV/XML/Parquet data formats, and cloud storage environments.
- Understanding of CDC mechanisms, data governance, and security best practices.
- Exposure to real-time or streaming ingestion (Kafka, EventHub) is beneficial.
- Experience working in Agile environments and delivering iterative outcomes.
- Ability to participate in and lead technical discussions.
- Interest or exposure to AI/ML workflows is a plus

Travel Expectations

Up to 5%


EOE/M/F/Vet/Disability

title: Manager, Data Engineering
description:
Your Opportunity at ARC’TERYX:

As a Manager, Data Engineering at Arc’teryx, you’ll lead a team responsible for our core data platform (including Databricks administration, ingestion frameworks, and QA frameworks) while ensuring technical excellence and delivery of data solutions. You’ll guide your team’s technical direction, develop engineering talent, and collaborate with stakeholders to deliver robust, reliable data infrastructure. You’ll balance hands‑on technical leadership with people management responsibilities, ensuring your team is well‑positioned to scale and support our data‑driven initiatives.

This position is based out of our North Vancouver office and is open to hybrid remote work. Candidates must be eligible to work in Canada.

Meet Your Future Team:

The data platform team builds and maintains the data infrastructure (including our Databricks environment, ingestion frameworks, and QA frameworks) that powers analytics, reporting, and data‑driven decision making across Arc’teryx’s digital platforms, retail operations, and business units. We work with cross‑functional agile squads to develop reliable data pipelines, improve data quality, build self‑serve analytics tools for our business stakeholders, and ensure timely access to accurate data for our analysts and data scientists.

If you were in the Manager, Data Engineering role now, here are some of the core activities you will be doing:

  • Leading and developing a team of data engineers while maintaining technical involvement
  • Guiding technical decisions and architecture for your team’s projects
  • Driving implementation of data engineering best practices and standards
  • Overseeing administration, scaling, and governance of our Databricks platform and the data pipelines built on it
  • Building and maintaining ingestion frameworks that onboard and standardize new data sources across the business
  • Collaborating with product managers and stakeholders to prioritize data initiatives
  • Managing team capacity, sprint planning, and delivery commitments
  • Coaching and mentoring data engineers in their technical and professional growth
  • Supporting hiring and onboarding of new team members
  • Establishing and maintaining QA frameworks to ensure data quality and reliability standards are met
  • Driving adoption of new tools and technologies within your team
  • Managing performance and career development for direct reports
  • Demonstrating Arc’teryx leadership code (Lead Self, Lead Others) in daily work

Here are some of the things you could be working on in the future:

  • Building and scaling high-performing data engineering teams to support organizational growth
  • Implementing structured career development frameworks for data engineering professionals
  • Leading the technical strategy for data platform modernization initiatives
  • Developing automated testing and CI/CD frameworks for data pipeline reliability
  • Establishing cross‑functional collaboration models between data and business teams
  • Standardizing data engineering practices across multiple development teams

Are you our next Manager, Data Engineering?

  • You have 8+ years of data engineering experience with 4+ years of team leadership
  • You have hands‑on experience managing data platform infrastructure, such as Databricks, ingestion frameworks, and QA frameworks
  • You have a combined strong technical background with emerging leadership capabilities
  • You have experience leading technical projects and mentoring engineers
  • You have excellent communication and stakeholder management skills
  • You are passionate about building strong engineering teams
  • You remain highly flexible and adaptable when faced with ambiguity
  • Your passion for technical leadership is paralleled by your passion for getting outside and living it

Compensation:

The salary range for this role is CAD$108,000 - CAD$142,000

Total Rewards

Most new team members join between the start and midpoint of the range, where you can contribute right away while continuing to grow your craft, your collaborations, and your impact at Arc’teryx. This range reflects market alignment and the scope of the role. Individual pay isdeterminedby your skills, experience, and level of responsibility.

We’recommitted to fair,equitable, and competitive pay, reviewed regularly to ensure internal alignment and market relevance.Transparency is part of how we follow through on our commitments and how we honour the value you bring to our team.

In addition to base pay, Arc’teryx supports people through benefits designed to sustain both work and life:

  • Financial wellbeing -RRSP matching and eligibility for Arc’teryx Annual Incentive Plan and access to Employee Stock Purchase program (ESPP) where applicable.
  • Time & Flexibilit** y** - Paid time off, wellness time, and No Wasted Day program(dedicated paid days to get outside & explore).
  • Family support - Parental leave top-up and a nesting period for new parents.
  • Growth, community & gear** **- Professional development opportunities, Arc’teryx Academies(outdoor skill-building events),Employee Belonging Councils, and access to employee discounts and Pro Deals(exclusive discounted pricing on gear).

*Eligibility for certain programs may vary by role.

Equal Opportunity

Arc’teryx is committed to actively creating and fostering a culture of inclusivity where voices are heard, people are seen, and values are respected. We care about the uniqueness of our applicants, employees, and guests, and we do so in a safe space fueled by curiosity and acceptance.

Creating an inclusive workplace is connected to our core value Do Right while also having the added benefit of helping make our business better. We believe inclusion helps us to create a healthier, happier workplace, drive creativity and innovation, and reflect the communities where we operate.

All applicants, employees, and guests can expect equality of opportunity and fair treatment in alignment with our values.

Leave it Better

We believe that the mountains transform us, that how we adventure matters, and that there’s always a better way.

Join us in creating positive change in ourselves, our communities, and the world.

Live it.Get out there - the mountains make us better

Disruptive evolution.In pursuit of better. Always.
